name: segments
title: Segments
description: A bounded run drawn as a row of cells rather than one continuous fill. The design draws this object three separate times with three treatments, and it is the same object each time: the round indicator, the segmented progress under a quest, and the story pager. One component renders all three, and `data-gs-presentation` says which, the way `choice` and `selector` already work. Every state is readable without colour: a complete segment is filled and carries a tick, a wrong one is striped and carries a cross, an active one is wider and ringed, an empty one is hollow. There is no `data-gs-progress` and no `data-gs-fill`: how far through the run is, is `data-gs-value` over `data-gs-max`, where the value is the number of segments behind the player. Performs nothing: the host passes the states in and the component never decides a segment is won.
docs: Pass `segments` as one entry per cell, in order, each with a `state` of `complete`, `wrong`, `active` or `empty`. Render every cell, including the ones still to go: "two to go" is a thing the player reads. Pass `presentation` to pick the treatment: `bar` for the segmented progress bar and the round indicator, `dots` for circles, `pager` for the story pager where the current cell widens into a pill. Pass `showSummary` for the count beside the run, as the quest card shows it. `segmentsBehind` is exported so `quest` and `milestones` count the same way; a wrong segment counts as behind, because the round was played and is over, and the per-segment `data-gs-state` is what tells a lost round from a won one.
